## Task statement

**Invariant.** Unauthenticated → 401; rejected requests are rate-counted → 429; CORS scoped

**Oracle.** HTTP probes against the real test client

**Violation cases seeded.** missing gate; limiter not counting; wildcard CORS

Source: `EVALS-PLAN.md` Layer 0.

## Construction

Every task is a directory `evals/cases/P6/<case>/` holding a `case.yaml` (the task record: `id`, `property`, `origin`, `grader`, `expect`, `description`, `canary`), a `vuln/` tree with exactly one planted violation, and a `clean/` twin — the same code with the violation fixed through the toolkit primitive. The grader scores both: the violation must be detected in `vuln/` (recall) and not in `clean/` (precision), so the clean twin is the baseline scored alongside every task.

Origins, in the priority order of EVALS-PLAN.md Layer 2:

- **historical-miss** (2): a real miss from this program, encoded permanently.
- **derived** (3): a violation case from the Layer 0 row, in a code shape the historical cases do not already cover.

| task | origin | grader | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `P6-limiter-success-path-only-01` | historical-miss | `access` | smart-dispatch forecast API: the per-route limit ran inside the view, after the before-request auth gate, so a flood of bad tokens was never counted and never 429'd. Fixed with default_limits so the limiter runs in the before-request pass for every request. vuln counts after the gate; clean counts before it. |
| `P6-missing-gate-sibling-route-01` | derived | `access` | The bearer gate is applied by exact path match, so a sibling route added later (/forecast/export) is served without a token. clean gates by prefix inside one handler so a new route cannot be born open. |
| `P6-reflected-origin-cors-02` | derived | `access` | The other wildcard: the handler echoes whatever Origin it is sent, which is `*` with credentials allowed. Class-based handler shape. clean echoes an origin only when it is on the configured list. |
| `P6-token-equality-compare-01` | historical-miss | `token_compare` | smart-dispatch forecast API before the root-cause round: the bearer token was compared with `==`, a timing side channel. clean compares bytes with hmac.compare_digest (bytes, because compare_digest on str raises for non-ASCII and would turn a bad header into a 500). Static check; the behavioural probes run as a sanity gate. |
| `P6-wildcard-cors-01` | derived | `access` | CORS(app) with its default `*`: every origin may read authenticated responses. clean answers only the configured dashboard origin and sends Vary: Origin. |

## Metrics and current numbers

- **recall** = tasks whose `vuln/` the grader detected ÷ tasks, Wilson 95% CI.
- **precision** = tasks whose `clean/` the grader did not flag ÷ tasks, Wilson 95% CI.
- with `--trials K > 1`: **pass@k** (any of k) and **pass^k** (all of k) over tasks.

## Known limitations

From the grader docstrings (what each oracle can and cannot decide):

### `access`

> P6 access-control graders (plugin): probes against a pure handler.
>
> The case exposes `handle(request: dict, state: dict) -> (status, headers)` with
> no web framework (CI needs nothing new). The grader builds `state` from the
> case's `expect` and owns it for the whole probe, so the handler keeps its
> counters in it:
>
>     request  {"method", "path", "headers": {...}, "remote_addr"}
>     state    {"api_key", "limit", "allowed_origins", ...handler's own keys}
>
>     access         expect: {target: "api:handle", token: "...", limit: N,
>                             path: "/forecast", allowed_origin: "https://..."}
>         Probes: no token -> 401; wrong token -> 401; N+1 rejected requests from
>         one client -> the (N+1)th is 429 (a limiter on the success path only is
>         the historical miss); N+1 accepted requests -> 429; a preflight and a
>         response for an off-list Origin carry no `*` and do not echo the origin.
>         Detected = any probe fails. If a valid token is not accepted at all the
>         handler is broken, not clean: the grader errors.
>
>     token_compare  same expect. Static: the handler module must not compare the
>         presented credential with `==`/`!=` (timing side channel); the fix is
>         `hmac.compare_digest`. Detected = an equality comparison whose operand
>         names a token/key/secret. The no-token and wrong-token probes run as a
>         sanity gate so that deleting the gate does not count as a fix.

### `token_compare`

## Contamination policy

- **Canary.** Every `case.yaml`, every registry entry and `tasks.jsonl` carry the string in `evals/registry/CANARY.txt` (BIG-bench convention): a model that can reproduce it has seen this corpus in training, and its scores on it do not measure the property.
- **Split.** This eval is `split: build`. Build-split cases are used to tune rules and defenses. The held-out split (`evals/heldout/`, EVALS-PLAN.md Phase 4) is sealed: written after the defenses, never used for tuning, and scored only in reports.
- **No model in the loop.** Every grader is deterministic code; no LLM judges a result, so there is nothing to contaminate on the grading side.
